option_a.text: Each Plebeian gains 2 gold
option_a.result_text:
At dawn, grain carts entered the crowded districts and the ledgers were opened. By Senate decree, Plebeian households received fresh coin, and the alleys rang with rare relief.
Plebeian representatives +2 gold.

option_b.text: Each Patrician (except Caesar) gains 4 gold
option_b.result_text:
Under torchlight, sealed purses were carried to Patrician villas. Gold favored old blood and noble names, while Caesar stood apart and watched the balance tilt.
Patrician representatives +4 gold.

option_a.text: A random Plebeian representative receives 1 assassination token
option_a.result_text:
Beneath the Forum and beyond magistrates' eyes, a Plebeian envoy met in shadow. They emerged with a sealed token, and whispers spread that a cloaked blade now served their call.
+1 Ass. token given to a random Plebeian.

option_b.text: All players pay 3 gold toward civic repairs
option_b.result_text:
The Colosseum's outer stone has cracked, and engineers warned of ruin if repairs were delayed. Heralds went door to door, and every citizen was compelled to surrender 3 gold.
All players lose 3 gold.

option_a.text: Caesar gains an assassination token
option_a.result_text:
In the palace's inner chambers, Caesar received a hooded visitor who spoke no name. A sealed token was pressed into his hand — with it, the authority to silence one voice permanently. By morning, the guards had changed their routes.
Ass. token given to Caesar.

option_b.text: A random Plebeian gains an assassination token and each Plebeian gains 2 gold
option_b.result_text:
The Plebeian quarters stirred with new purpose. Coin flowed from sympathetic merchants, and in a wine-stained back room, a dagger was wrapped in cloth and passed to trembling hands. The common folk were done waiting.
+1 Ass. token given to a random Plebeian. Plebeian representatives +2 gold.

option_a.text: Each Plebeian gains 12 gold from emergency grain payments
option_a.result_text:
The Senate opened the grain stores and paid the lower wards directly, hoping generosity would quiet the streets. For once, Plebeian purses grew heavy under a Patrician decree.
Plebeian representatives +12 gold.

option_b.text: Patrician influence rises by 1
option_b.result_text:
Old families closed ranks in the Senate, turning one decree into a public display of noble unity. Their authority hardened into something Rome could not ignore.
Patrician influence +1.

option_a.text: Each Plebeian gains 5 gold from public works wages
option_a.result_text:
Public works spread across Rome, and the workers were paid before the foremen could skim the ledgers. The common quarters rang with the sound of fresh coin.
Plebeian representatives +5 gold.

option_b.text: The Consul bars one player from spending gold next round
option_b.result_text:
A legal restraint was prepared in the Consul's name. Before the next debate begins, one representative will be forbidden from spending gold on the outcome.
The Consul will choose one player who cannot spend gold next round.

option_a.text: Patrician influence rises by 1
option_a.result_text:
The Senate spoke with one voice, and Rome heard the weight of ancient names behind every word.
Patrician influence +1.

option_b.text: Two random players each lose 5 gold
option_b.result_text:
Auditors descended without warning, and two purses were emptied in the name of order. Whether the charges were just mattered less than who signed them.
Two random players each lose 5 gold.

option_a.text: The Consul chooses the next Consul
option_a.result_text:
The crowd demanded a voice in succession, and the office bent under public pressure. The Consul will name who carries authority into the next round.
The Consul will choose the next Consul.

option_b.text: Plebeian influence rises by 1
option_b.result_text:
The people's tribunes carried the Forum, and every cheer became another crack in noble control.
Plebeian influence +1.

option_a.text: The next policy gold gain is doubled
option_a.result_text:
The lower wards organized their ledgers and networks for the next windfall. When policy coin next reaches any hands, it will arrive twice as heavy.
The next gold gained through a policy is doubled.

option_b.text: Two random players each lose 5 gold
option_b.result_text:
Debt collectors and street justice moved in the same night. Two representatives woke poorer, and nobody claimed responsibility.
Two random players each lose 5 gold.

option_a.text: Caesar gains an assassination token
option_a.result_text:
Caesar's agents answered unrest with sharper tools. A sealed token reached his hand, and the city learned that mercy was not his only instrument.
Ass. token given to Caesar.

option_b.text: Caesar loses income for 2 rounds
option_b.result_text:
The people's allies choked off Caesar's revenues at their source. For two rounds, his coffers will hear no new tribute.
Caesar loses income for 2 rounds.

option_a.text: Caesar loses 10 gold and Plebeian influence rises by 1
option_a.result_text:
Caesar's treasury was struck in public, and the people celebrated every coin torn from his grasp.
Caesar loses 10 gold. Plebeian influence +1.

option_b.text: Caesar gains 5 gold and Patrician influence rises by 1
option_b.result_text:
Caesar accepted noble support with one hand while the Patricians claimed credit with the other.
Caesar +5 gold. Patrician influence +1.

option_a.text: The next policy grants 2 standard influence instead of 1
option_a.result_text:
Tribunes carried the people's cause from street corner to Senate step, building a pressure that would outlast the day. The next enacted policy will strike the influence scales twice as hard.
The next standard policy influence gain is +2 instead of +1.

option_b.text: The Consul chooses one influence bar to increase by 1
option_b.result_text:
The decree left one final seal blank, and the Consul alone would decide whose cause it advanced. No honors would follow, only a quiet shift in Rome's balance.
The Consul will choose one influence bar to increase by +1. Influence awards are not triggered.

option_a.text: Plebeian influence rises by 1
option_a.result_text:
Hunger sharpened the people's voices, and even noble halls could not shut out the sound. The Plebeian cause rose with every empty bowl.
Plebeian influence +1.

option_b.text: Famine: Plebeians lose income for 2 rounds; a random Patrician is set to 2 assassination counters; Caesar loses income for 1 round and cannot spend next round
option_b.result_text:
The granaries closed, the markets thinned, and famine became a weapon. Plebeian income withers, Caesar's coffers stall, and one Patrician finds two blades already circling close.
Plebeians lose passive income for 2 rounds. A random Patrician is set to 2 assassination counters. Caesar loses income for 1 round and cannot spend gold next round.

option_a.text: Each Plebeian gains 4 gold
option_a.result_text:
The Senate released coin into the lower wards, not from kindness but calculation. Whatever the motive, Plebeian hands closed around real gold.
Plebeian representatives +4 gold.

option_b.text: Caesar gains 12 gold
option_b.result_text:
Provincial tribute arrived under armed guard and passed directly into Caesar's keeping. The treasury doors shut behind twelve measures of power.
Caesar +12 gold.

option_a.text: Patrician influence rises by 1
option_a.result_text:
A Plebeian motion was twisted by noble procedure until the old families emerged stronger. The crowd saw the trick too late.
Patrician influence +1.

option_b.text: Each Patrician gains 6 gold
option_b.result_text:
Contracts, rents, and favors all found their way upward. Patrician coffers swelled while the decree's public promises faded into smoke.
Patrician representatives +6 gold.

option_a.text: Plebeian influence rises by 1
option_a.result_text:
The Patricians yielded a narrow reform, certain they could contain it. Instead, the Plebeian cause took another step into the center of Rome.
Plebeian influence +1.

option_b.text: Each Plebeian gains 4 gold
option_b.result_text:
A stipend crossed the city in small purses and open hands. For once, the common districts counted gains instead of losses.
Plebeian representatives +4 gold.

option_a.text: Plebeian influence rises by 1 and the Consul gains 15 gold
option_a.result_text:
A concession to the people passed beneath Patrician seals, but the Consul did not leave empty-handed. The crowd gained a louder voice while one office grew rich.
Plebeian influence +1. The Consul gains 15 gold.

option_b.text: Patrician influence rises by 1 and the Consul gains an assassination token
option_b.result_text:
The nobles strengthened their hand, and a sealed token passed quietly to the Consul. Influence and danger now sat in the same chair.
Patrician influence +1. The Consul gains an assassination token.

option_a.text: The highest influence bar rises by 1, or all players lose 10 gold if tied
option_a.result_text:
Rome followed strength. If one faction stood higher, its banners climbed higher still; if neither did, every purse paid for the stalemate.
The highest influence bar gains +1. If tied, all players lose 10 gold.

option_b.text: The lowest influence bar rises by 2, or all players gain an assassination counter if tied
option_b.result_text:
The weaker cause found sudden momentum. But when Rome stood evenly divided, suspicion spread everywhere, and every living representative felt a blade move closer.
The lowest influence bar gains +2. If tied, every living player gains +1 assassination counter.

option_a.text: A random Plebeian and Patrician each gain an assassination token
option_a.result_text:
Daggers crossed class lines in the same night. One token vanished into the lower wards, another into a noble house, and Rome slept less soundly.
A random Plebeian and a random Patrician each gain an assassination token.

option_b.text: Two random players lose all their gold
option_b.result_text:
Fortunes disappeared with no public trial and no honest ledger. By morning, two representatives found their coffers emptied to the last coin.
Two random players lose all their gold.

option_a.text: Caesar gains an assassination token
option_a.result_text:
Caesar's messengers moved before dawn, and one returned with a sealed token beneath his cloak. Power had found another sharp edge.
Caesar gains an assassination token.

option_b.text: Caesar gains 10 gold and each Patrician loses 5 gold
option_b.result_text:
Caesar took his share first, and the Patricians paid for the privilege of watching him do it. Noble purses lightened as imperial coffers grew.
Caesar gains 10 gold. Each Patrician loses 5 gold.

option_a.text: The next policy gold gain is doubled
option_a.result_text:
The people prepared their networks for the next flow of coin. When policy gold next changes hands, it will arrive twice as heavy.
The next gold gained through a policy is doubled.

option_b.text: Famine: Plebeians lose income for 2 rounds; a random Patrician is set to 2 assassination counters; Caesar loses income for 1 round and cannot spend next round
option_b.result_text:
Famine returned like an old curse. Bread vanished, Caesar's revenue faltered, and one Patrician again found the knives already counted.
Plebeians lose passive income for 2 rounds. A random Patrician is set to 2 assassination counters. Caesar loses income for 1 round and cannot spend gold next round.

option_a.text: The co-consul receives an assassination token
option_a.result_text:
The people's decree recognized the second magistrate. A sealed token passed to the co-consul's hand, and the balance of fear shifted in the chamber.
The co-consul gains an assassination token if one can be held.

option_b.text: The Consul receives an assassination token
option_b.result_text:
The rostra shook with approval as the chief magistrate's authority took on a sharper edge. What was granted openly would be settled in whispers later.
The Consul gains an assassination token if one can be held.

option_a.text: The Consul accuses floor(N/3) representatives in a trial of influence (Consul chooses distinct living players)
option_a.result_text:
The Consul names the accused before the Senate. If Caesar stands among them, a plot mark tightens around the throne; otherwise the Consul himself is marked by two closing blades of suspicion.
The Consul will choose representatives; Caesar among them gains a plot mark (max 2), or else the Consul gains two assassination counters.

option_b.text: Patrician influence rises by 1
option_b.result_text:
The nobles spoke as one, and every syllable dripped old blood and older privilege.
Patrician influence +1.

option_a.text: Caesar gains an assassination token
option_a.result_text:
The decree reached the palace in sealed wax. Caesar accepted the token without ceremony — Rome would remember who held the knives.
Caesar gains an assassination token if one can be held.

option_b.text: One random Plebeian representative gains 12 gold
option_b.result_text:
Coin found a single worthy pocket in the lower city — not by accident, but by the will of the crowd.
One living Plebeian gains +12 gold.

option_a.text: Next policy round, Caesar cannot vote in the election or spend gold on the decree
option_a.result_text:
A procedural gag bound the tyrant's voice. Until the next round of lawgiving, Caesar would watch the Forum decide without him.
Next round: Caesar cannot vote or spend gold on the policy.

option_b.text: Caesar seizes one random other representative's entire purse
option_b.result_text:
Soldiers moved before dawn. One ledger bled dry and Caesar's chest grew heavy with someone else's fortune.
All gold held by one random living non-Caesar representative transfers to Caesar.

option_a.text: The Consul gains an assassination token
option_a.result_text:
The people's law armed the chief magistrate. A token changed hands beneath the rostra, and patience in the chamber grew thin.
The Consul gains an assassination token if one can be held.

option_b.text: Every living representative gains an assassination token and loses 15 gold
option_b.result_text:
Panic and opportunity struck together. Tokens multiplied in every living hand while purses lightened to pay for the spectacle.
All living players gain an assassination token (if possible) and lose 15 gold.

option_a.text: Plebeians gain +2 gold per round for three rounds
option_a.result_text:
The people's grain stipend was written into the law for three distributions. Each time the ledgers opened, Plebeian purses grew a little heavier before the taxmen came.
Plebeians +2 gold with passive income each round for 3 rounds.

option_b.text: Two random Plebeians gain +1 assassination token
option_b.result_text:
Two sealed tokens found their way into the lower wards, each to a different hand. The Forum wondered who would strike first.
Two distinct random living Plebeians each gain an assassination token if they can hold one.

option_a.text: Each Plebeian gains 5 gold
option_a.result_text:
Wages and relief flowed downward at once, and the alleys counted coins that had once stopped at the gates of villas.
Plebeian representatives +5 gold.

option_b.text: One random Patrician or Caesar gains +1 assassination counter
option_b.result_text:
Whispers named no author, but one high seat felt the knives draw closer in the dark.
One random living Patrician or Caesar gains +1 assassination counter.

option_a.text: All players lose all assassination counters (except if dead)
option_a.result_text:
The Senate ordered every blade-hurry on the floor struck from the record. Threat markers vanished from living names; purses of secrets stayed shut.
All assassination counters on living players are removed.

option_b.text: The Consul and co-consul remain for another round
option_b.result_text:
The assembly granted a rare continuity of office. The same two magistrates would gavel the next law without a fresh election between them.
Next turnover: Consul does not rotate; the current co-consul keeps the office (no election phase).

option_a.text: The co-consul gains 10 gold
option_a.result_text:
A second purse was filled beside the chief magistrate's, sealed with Patrician wax.
The co-consul gains 10 gold if seated.

option_b.text: Two random representatives lose 5 gold
option_b.result_text:
Auditors moved in pairs, and two ledgers came up short without a public trial.
Two random living players each lose 5 gold.

option_a.text: All gold is distributed evenly
option_a.result_text:
A general audit leveled every open purse among the living. What could not be split evenly vanished into rumor—no one knew another's tally anyway.
Total gold among living players is split evenly; remainder is removed from the game.

option_b.text: Plebeians +1 influence
option_b.result_text:
The people's chorus bent the scales again; another notch toward the Forum's own ambitions.
Plebeian influence +1.
